questions.question: What is the main cause of acid rain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Acid rain** is caused by a chemical reaction that begins when compounds like **sulfur dioxide (SO2)** and **nitrogen oxides (NOx)** are released into the atmosphere.

• These substances rise high into the air, where they react with **water (H2O)**, **oxygen**, and other chemicals to form **sulfuric acid** and **nitric acid**.

• The primary source of these pollutants is the burning of **fossil fuels** in **power plants**, **industrial factories**, and **motor vehicles**.

• **Sulfur dioxide** and **nitrogen oxides** are highly soluble in water and can be transported over long distances by wind before falling to the ground as rain, snow, fog, or dust.

• While **Carbon monoxide** and **methane** are significant greenhouse gases contributing to global warming, they are not the primary precursors of acid rain. **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)** are mainly responsible for **ozone layer depletion**, and **lead and mercury** are toxic heavy metals but do not cause acidity in precipitation.

**Additional Information__**

• Normal rainwater has a **pH** of about 5.6 because **carbon dioxide** dissolves in it to form weak **carbonic acid**. Acid rain typically has a **pH** between 4.2 and 4.4.

• The chemical process involves the formation of H₂SO₄ (Sulfuric acid) and HNO₃ (Nitric acid).

• Acid rain has devastating effects on **aquatic ecosystems**, as it leaches **aluminum** from soil into lakes and streams, which is toxic to fish.

• It also damages **forests** by removing essential nutrients from the soil and harms **man-made structures**, particularly those made of **limestone** or **marble** (calcium carbonate), through chemical weathering.

• A famous example of acid rain damage is the yellowing of the **Taj Mahal** in India due to emissions from nearby industries in the **Taj Trapezium Zone**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the provisions of the POSH Act, 2013?

options.text: The POSH Act, 2013 is designed to prevent child marriage in India.
The POSH Act, 2013 provides protection against sexual harassment of women at the workplace.
The POSH Act, 2013 governs the regulation of orphanages across India.
The POSH Act, 2013 focuses on the harassment of domestic workers.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The POSH Act, 2013 provides protection against sexual harassment of women at the workplace**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act**, commonly known as the **POSH Act**, was enacted by the **Ministry of Women and Child Development** in **2013** to ensure a safe and secure environment for women in their professional lives.

• **Statement 1**: The **POSH Act, 2013** is designed to prevent child marriage in India. This statement is incorrect because the prevention of child marriage is governed by the **Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006**, which sets the legal age for marriage. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• **Statement 2**: The **POSH Act, 2013** provides protection against sexual harassment of women at the workplace. This is the fundamental purpose of the legislation, which seeks to uphold the **fundamental right** of women to equality and a dignified livelihood as guaranteed under **Article 14, 15, and 21** of the **Constitution of India**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***

• **Statement 3**: The **POSH Act, 2013** governs the regulation of orphanages across India. This statement is incorrect as the care, protection, and regulation of orphanages and children in need are handled under the **Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

• **Statement 4**: The **POSH Act, 2013** focuses on the harassment of domestic workers. While the act specifically includes **domestic workers** within its definition of an **aggrieved woman** and a **dwelling place** as a **workplace**, the act is a broad legislation covering all types of workplaces, not just domestic settings. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct but is a specific subset of the broader protection mentioned in statement 2.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Vishaka Guidelines**: The **POSH Act** is rooted in the **Vishaka Guidelines** formulated by the **Supreme Court of India** in **1997** following the landmark case of **Vishaka vs. State of Rajasthan**. These guidelines remained the law of the land for **16 years** until the formal act was passed in **2013**.

• **Internal Committee (IC)**: Every employer who has **10 or more employees** is legally mandated to constitute an **Internal Committee** at each branch or office to receive and redress complaints of sexual harassment.

• **Local Committee (LC)**: For establishments with fewer than **10 employees**, or if the complaint is against the employer himself, the **District Officer** (usually the **District Magistrate** or **Additional District Magistrate**) is required to constitute a **Local Committee** in every district.

• **Definition of Workplace**: The act defines **workplace** very broadly, including **private sector organizations**, **government bodies**, **hospitals**, **sports institutes**, **stadiums**, and any place visited by the employee during the course of employment, including **transportation** provided by the employer.

• **Definition of Sexual Harassment**: It includes unwelcome acts such as **physical contact**, a demand or **request for sexual favors**, **sexually colored remarks**, showing **pornography**, or any other unwelcome physical, verbal, or non-verbal conduct of a sexual nature.

**Important Points__**

• **Aggrieved Woman**: Under the **POSH Act**, an **aggrieved woman** is defined as a woman of **any age**, whether employed or not, who alleges to have been subjected to any act of sexual harassment by the respondent. This includes **regular**, **temporary**, **ad hoc**, or **daily wage** employees.

• **Complaint Timeline**: A written complaint must be filed with the **Internal Committee** or **Local Committee** within a period of **3 months** from the date of the incident. In the case of a series of incidents, it must be within **3 months** from the date of the last incident.

• **Redressal Process**: Before starting an inquiry, the committee can, at the request of the woman, attempt to settle the matter through **conciliation**. However, no **monetary settlement** can be made the basis of such conciliation. If conciliation is not possible, a formal inquiry is conducted within **90 days**.

• **SHe-Box Portal**: To facilitate the registration of complaints, the **Government of India** launched the **Sexual Harassment electronic Box (SHe-Box)**, an online portal that allows women in both **public and private sectors** to report incidents directly to the **Ministry of Women and Child Development**.

• **Penalties**: Non-compliance with the provisions of the act, such as failure to constitute an **Internal Committee**, can result in a fine of up to **50,000 rupees** for the employer, and repeated offenses can lead to the **cancellation of the business license**.
</ul

questions.question: The Pravasi Bharatiya Divas marks which Indian leader's return from South Africa?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (PBD)** is celebrated in India on **9th January** to mark the contribution of the overseas Indian community to the development of India.

• The date **9th January** was chosen because it was on this day in **1915** that **Mahatma Gandhi**, the greatest **Pravasi**, returned to **India** from **South Africa**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Mahatma Gandhi.***

• The event was first celebrated in **2003**. It was an annual event until **2015**, after which the government decided to celebrate it **biennially** (once every two years).

• The concept of PBD was based on the recommendations of the **High Level Committee (HLC)** on the Indian Diaspora set up by the Government of India under the chairmanship of **Dr. L. M. Singhvi**.

• The other leaders mentioned in the options, such as **Lala Lajpat Rai**, **Sarojini Naidu**, and **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**, were prominent figures in the Indian freedom struggle, but their returns or specific anniversaries are not the basis for this commemorative day. ***Hence, options 1, 2, and 3 are incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Mahatma Gandhi in South Africa:** Gandhi spent approximately **21 years** in **South Africa** (from **1893** to **1914**). It was during this period that he developed his philosophy of **Satyagraha** (non-violent resistance) and fought against racial discrimination. He arrived at **Apollo Bunder** in **Mumbai** on **January 9, 1915**.

• **17th Pravasi Bharatiya Divas:** The **17th PBD Convention** was held from **8th to 10th January 2023** in **Indore, Madhya Pradesh**. The theme for the 2023 convention was **'Diaspora: Reliable partners for India’s progress in Amrit Kaal'**.

• **Pravasi Bharatiya Samman Award (PBSA):** This is the **highest honour** conferred by the **President of India** on **Non-Resident Indians (NRIs)**, **Persons of Indian Origin (PIOs)**, or organizations established by them, to recognize their outstanding achievements and contributions.

• **Nodal Ministry:** The **Ministry of External Affairs (MEA)** of the **Government of India** is the primary body responsible for organizing the PBD conventions and managing the engagement with the Indian diaspora.

• **Regional PBDs:** In addition to the main convention, **Regional Pravasi Bharatiya Divas** events are organized outside India to reach out to those diaspora members who cannot attend the main event in India.

**Important Points__**

• **Lala Lajpat Rai:** Often called **Punjab Kesari**, he was a leader of the **Lal-Bal-Pal** trio and played a major role in the **Swadeshi Movement**. He passed away in **1928** after being injured during a protest against the **Simon Commission**.

• **Sarojini Naidu:** Known as the **Nightingale of India**, she was the first Indian woman to serve as the **President of the Indian National Congress** (1925) and the first woman **Governor** of an Indian state (**United Provinces**). Her birthday, **February 13**, is celebrated as **National Women's Day** in India.

• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak:** A prominent nationalist and teacher, he was one of the first leaders of the **Indian Independence Movement**. He is famous for his quote, **'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it!'**. He founded the **Home Rule League** in **1916**.

• **Significance of PBD:** The day provides a platform for the **overseas Indian community** to engage with the government and people of their ancestral land, fostering **networking** and **investment** opportunities while celebrating their cultural roots.

questions.question: To modify the magnitude of an alternating voltage without altering its frequency, which principle is applied in the functioning of a transformer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mutual induction**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• A **transformer** is a static electrical device that transfers electrical energy between two or more circuits through **electromagnetic induction**.

• The fundamental principle behind the operation of a transformer is **Mutual Induction**. This occurs when a changing magnetic flux produced by the **primary winding** links with the **secondary winding**, inducing an electromotive force (EMF) in it.

• The transformer modifies the **magnitude of alternating voltage** (stepping it up or down) while keeping the **frequency** of the power constant.

• **Self-induction** is the phenomenon where a change in current in a single coil induces an EMF in that same coil. While it occurs in the primary winding, the transfer of energy to the secondary is due to mutual induction.

• **Electromagnetic radiation** involves the emission of energy as waves (like radio waves), which is not the mechanism for power transformation in a transformer.

• **Capacitive coupling** involves the transfer of energy through an electric field between two points of a circuit, which is different from the magnetic coupling used in transformers.

**Additional Information__**

• A transformer consists of two inductive coils (**Primary** and **Secondary**) which are electrically separated but magnetically linked through a **ferromagnetic core**.

• The relationship between the voltages and the number of turns in the coils is given by the formula: (V_p)/(V_s) = (N_p)/(N_s) , where **V** represents voltage and **N** represents the number of turns.

• **Step-up transformers** increase the output voltage (Ns > Np), whereas **Step-down transformers** decrease the output voltage (Ns < Np).

• Transformers operate only on **Alternating Current (AC)** because **Direct Current (DC)** does not produce the changing magnetic flux necessary for induction.

• The efficiency of modern transformers is very high, often exceeding **95 percent**, as there are no moving parts and thus no mechanical friction losses.
</ul

questions.question:
**Consider the following statements about market equilibrium:****Statement I: In equilibrium, the quantity that all firms wish to sell equals the quantity all consumers want to buy.
Statement II: Excess supply exists when the market demand is greater than the market supply.
Which of the above statements is/are correct**?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Statement I is correct**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Market Equilibrium** is defined as a situation in the market where the **Quantity Demanded** of a commodity is exactly equal to its **Quantity Supplied**. At this point, there is no inherent tendency for the price to change, and the market is said to be cleared.

• **Statement I** states that in equilibrium, the quantity that all firms wish to sell equals the quantity all consumers want to buy. This is the fundamental condition for equilibrium in a competitive market. At the **Equilibrium Price**, the intentions of buyers and sellers are perfectly synchronized. ***Hence, Statement I is correct.***

• **Statement II** suggests that **Excess Supply** exists when market demand is greater than market supply. This is economically inaccurate. **Excess Supply**, also known as a **Surplus**, occurs when the **Quantity Supplied** exceeds the **Quantity Demanded** at the prevailing market price. This usually happens when the market price is set above the equilibrium level.

• When the **Market Demand** is greater than the **Market Supply**, the condition is known as **Excess Demand** or a **Shortage**. This typically occurs when the market price is below the equilibrium level, leading to competition among buyers that eventually pushes the price upward. ***Hence, Statement II is incorrect.***

• The point where the **Demand Curve** and the **Supply Curve** intersect on a graph represents the **Market Equilibrium**, determining both the **Equilibrium Price** and the **Equilibrium Quantity**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Law of Demand**: This law states that, keeping other factors constant (**Ceteris Paribus**), there is an inverse relationship between the price of a good and its **Quantity Demanded**. As the price falls, consumers are willing to buy more.

• **Law of Supply**: This law indicates a direct relationship between price and **Quantity Supplied**. As the market price increases, producers are incentivized to offer more of the good for sale to increase their **Profit Margins**.

• **Price Mechanism**: This refers to the process by which the forces of **Supply and Demand** interact to determine the prices of goods and services. It acts as a signal for resource allocation in a **Market Economy**.

• **Market Clearing**: A market is said to clear when the price adjusts such that the quantity supplied equals the quantity demanded, leaving no **Unsold Inventory** and no **Unmet Demand**.

• **Equilibrium Shifts**: Changes in external factors such as **Consumer Income**, **Technology**, **Input Prices**, or **Government Policy** can cause the demand or supply curves to shift, leading to a new **Market Equilibrium**.

**Important Points__**

• **Adam Smith**: The father of modern economics described the self-regulating nature of the market as the **Invisible Hand**. He argued that individuals pursuing their own self-interest in a free market lead to an efficient **Market Equilibrium**.

• **Alfred Marshall**: The **19th-century** economist **Alfred Marshall** is credited with standardizing the use of **Supply and Demand** diagrams to illustrate **Market Equilibrium** in his seminal work, **'Principles of Economics' (1890)**.

• **Price Floors and Ceilings**: Government interventions like a **Price Floor** (minimum price) can lead to persistent **Excess Supply**, while a **Price Ceiling** (maximum price) can lead to chronic **Excess Demand** or black markets.

• **Stability of Equilibrium**: An equilibrium is considered stable if, following a small **Displacement**, market forces (the **Price Mechanism**) push the price and quantity back toward the original equilibrium point.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are **correct**?**Statement I:** Intermediate goods are goods used as inputs in the production of other goods**Statement II:** Capital goods are durable goods used in production that do not get transformed into the final product.

options.text: Both statements I and II are correct
Both statements I and II are incorrect
Statement I is correct, Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, Statement II is correct

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both statements I and II are correct**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Intermediate goods** refer to those goods that are used as **inputs** in the **production** of other goods or services. These goods are either entirely consumed or undergo transformation during the production process within the same **accounting year**. For example, **flour** used by a **baker** to bake **bread** or **steel** used in the **manufacturing** of a **car** are intermediate goods. ***Hence, Statement I is correct.***

• **Capital goods** are **durable** goods used in the **production** process that do not get transformed into the **final product**. These are **fixed assets** of the producers, such as **machinery**, **equipment**, **tools**, and **factory buildings**. They can be used repeatedly in the production process for several years and do not lose their identity in the final output. ***Hence, Statement II is correct.***

• The classification of a good as **intermediate** or **capital** depends on its **end-use**. If a **machine** is purchased for **resale** by a dealer, it is treated as an **intermediate good**, but if it is purchased by a **factory** for use in production, it is a **capital good**.

• In **National Income** accounting, the value of **intermediate goods** is not included separately to avoid the problem of **double counting**, as their value is already merged into the value of the **final goods**. **Capital goods**, however, are included as they constitute **investment**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Final Goods**: These are goods meant for **final consumption** by households or for **final investment** by firms. They are not intended for further **resale** or **transformation** within the same **year**.

• **Consumption Goods**: These are **final goods** that satisfy **human wants** directly. They are categorized into **durable goods** (e.g., **televisions**, **refrigerators**), **semi-durable goods** (e.g., **clothes**, **crockery**), **non-durable goods** (e.g., **milk**, **bread**), and **services** (e.g., **education**, **healthcare**).

• **Gross Investment**: This refers to the total addition made to the **capital stock** of an **economy** during a given period. It includes **Net Investment** and **Depreciation**.

• **Depreciation**: Also known as the **consumption of fixed capital**, it represents the loss in the value of **fixed assets** due to normal **wear and tear**, **accidental damages**, or **expected obsolescence** over a period of **time**.

• **Inventory**: This includes the stock of **finished goods**, **semi-finished goods**, and **raw materials** held by a **business** at a specific point in **time**. Change in **inventory** is considered a part of **investment**.

**Important Points__**

• The **Value-Added Method** of calculating **GDP** involves subtracting the value of **intermediate consumption** from the **Value of Output**. This ensures that only the **contribution** of each **production unit** is counted.

• **Capital goods** are a sub-category of **producer goods**. While all **capital goods** are **producer goods**, not all **producer goods** are **capital goods** (as raw materials are also producer goods but are not capital goods).

• In the **Indian context**, the **National Statistical Office (NSO)**, which operates under the **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)**, is the nodal agency for the **classification** and **estimation** of these **economic aggregates**.

• The **Circular Flow of Income** demonstrates how **expenditure** on **final goods** (including **capital goods**) becomes **income** for the **factors of production**, while **intermediate goods** remain within the **production boundary**.
</ul

questions.question:
Instructions: Read the Assertion (A) and Reason (R) carefully. Choose the correct option:
Assertion (A): India launched the South Asian Satellite (SAS) in 2017 for use by SAARC nations.
Reason (R): The SAS was launched from the Sriharikota spaceport, and its terminals were installed in all SAARC countries.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A is true, but R is false**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Assertion (A)** states that **India** launched the **South Asian Satellite (SAS)** in **2017** for use by **SAARC** nations. This statement is **correct**. The satellite, also known as **GSAT-9**, was launched on **May 5, 2017**, as a gift from **India** to its neighboring countries to bolster communication and regional cooperation.

• The **South Asian Satellite** was a brainchild of Prime Minister **Narendra Modi**, who proposed the idea during the **18th SAARC Summit** held in **Nepal** in **2014**. The project aimed to provide various communication applications to **South Asian** countries.

• **Reason (R)** states that the **SAS** was launched from the **Sriharikota** spaceport, and its terminals were installed in all **SAARC** countries. This statement is **incorrect**. While the satellite was indeed launched from the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre** in **Sriharikota** using the **GSLV-F09** rocket, it does not serve all **SAARC** nations.

• **Pakistan**, a key member of **SAARC**, decided to opt out of the project, claiming it had its own space program and technical capabilities. Consequently, the satellite benefits only seven out of the eight **SAARC** members: **India**, **Afghanistan**, **Bangladesh**, **Bhutan**, **Maldives**, **Nepal**, and **Sri Lanka**. Therefore, terminals were not installed in **Pakistan**. ***Hence, statement A is true, but statement R is false.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Technical Specifications:** The **GSAT-9** is a **Geostationary Communication Satellite** developed by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**. It weighs approximately **2,230 kg** and is equipped with **12 Ku-band transponders**.

• **Mission Life:** The satellite has an intended mission life of more than **12 years**. It is positioned at **48 degrees East** longitude in the geostationary orbit.

• **Applications:** The **South Asian Satellite** provides a wide range of services, including **Tele-education**, **Tele-medicine**, **Disaster Management Support**, **Broadcasting** (DTH), and **VSAT** (Very Small Aperture Terminal) connectivity for banking and government networks.

• **Regional Cooperation:** The project is a significant part of **India**'s **'Neighborhood First'** policy. By providing the satellite services free of charge to participating nations, **India** aimed to strengthen diplomatic ties and aid the socio-economic development of the **South Asian** region.

• **SAARC Overview:** The **South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC)** was established in **1985**. Its secretariat is located in **Kathmandu, Nepal**. The member states include **Afghanistan**, **Bangladesh**, **Bhutan**, **India**, **Maldives**, **Nepal**, **Pakistan**, and **Sri Lanka**.

**Important Points__**

• **Cost of Project:** The total cost of the **South Asian Satellite** project was approximately **₹235 crore** (around **USD 36 million**), which was entirely funded by the **Government of India**. The participating nations only had to bear the cost of ground station infrastructure and maintenance.

• **Launch Vehicle:** The **GSLV-F09** (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle) used for this mission featured the indigenous **Cryogenic Upper Stage (CUS)**, marking another milestone for **ISRO**'s heavy-lift capabilities.

• **Ground Terminals:** **India** assisted participating countries like **Bhutan** and **Afghanistan** in setting up the necessary ground stations and terminals to receive and transmit data via the **GSAT-9** satellite.

• **Strategic Importance:** Beyond its functional uses, the satellite serves as a strategic tool for **India** to counter the growing influence of other global powers in the **Indian Ocean** and **South Asian** region by providing essential space-based infrastructure.

questions.question: How many gold medals did India win in Wrestling at the Birmingham 2022 CWG?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• India's wrestling contingent delivered an exceptional performance at the **Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games**, winning a total of **12 medals** across various weight categories.

• Out of the 12 medals won in wrestling, **6 were gold medals**, 1 was silver, and 5 were bronze.

• The **six gold medalists** who brought glory to India in wrestling were:
 
 
• **Bajrang Punia**: Men's Freestyle 65kg
 
• **Sakshi Malik**: Women's Freestyle 62kg
 
• **Deepak Punia**: Men's Freestyle 86kg
 
• **Ravi Kumar Dahiya**: Men's Freestyle 57kg
 
• **Vinesh Phogat**: Women's Freestyle 53kg
 
• **Naveen Malik**: Men's Freestyle 74kg
 

• Wrestling was the **most successful sport** for India at the 2022 Games, with every single member of the 12-member wrestling squad winning a medal.

**Additional Information__**

• The **Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games** (officially known as the XXII Commonwealth Games) were held in **England**, United Kingdom.

• India finished in **fourth position** in the overall medal tally, securing a total of **61 medals** (22 Gold, 16 Silver, and 23 Bronze).

• **Vinesh Phogat** achieved a historic feat by becoming the first Indian woman to win **three consecutive gold medals** at the Commonwealth Games (Glasgow 2014, Gold Coast 2018, and Birmingham 2022).

• The lone **silver medal** in wrestling was won by **Anshu Malik** in the Women's Freestyle 57kg category.

• The **bronze medalists** in wrestling included **Divya Kakran**, **Mohit Grewal**, **Pooja Gehlot**, **Pooja Sihag**, and **Deepak Nehra**.
</ul

questions.question: What major accomplishment by Satwik and Chirag in 2023 earned them the prestigious Khel Ratna Award?

options.text: Securing a silver medal at the World Badminton Championships
Winning the gold medal at the Asian Games
Clinching a bronze medal at the Commonwealth Games
Earning the National Badminton Championship title

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Winning the gold medal at the Asian Games**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• The star Indian badminton duo, **Satwiksairaj Rankireddy** and **Chirag Shetty**, were honored with the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award** for the year **2023**.

• Their most significant achievement in 2023 was clinching the **gold medal** at the **Asian Games** in **Hangzhou**, which was India's **first-ever gold** in badminton at the continental event.

• The pair demonstrated remarkable consistency throughout the year, defeating top-seeded global pairs to secure their historic victory in the final against **South Korea**.

• The **Khel Ratna** is the highest sporting honor in India, and their selection was based on a spectacular season where they also reached the **World No. 1** ranking in the **BWF** men's doubles category.

• While they have won medals at the **World Championships** and **Commonwealth Games** in previous years, the 2023 award specifically recognized their unprecedented success at the Asian Games and on the **BWF World Tour** during that calendar year.

**Additional Information__**

• In 2023, **Satwik-Chirag** also won the **Indonesia Open** (a Super 1000 event), the **Korea Open**, and the **Swiss Open**.

• The **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award** was previously known as the **Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award** before being renamed in **2021**.

• The duo played a pivotal role in India's historic **Thomas Cup** victory in **2022**, which set the stage for their dominant 2023 season.

• The awards are presented annually by the **President of India** at the **Rashtrapati Bhavan** to recognize excellence in sports.
</ul

questions.question: The Atal Pension Yojana (APY) aims to provide pension benefits to which segment of the population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Unorganized sector workers**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Atal Pension Yojana (APY)** was officially launched on **9th May 2015** by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** in **Kolkata**, **West Bengal**. The scheme is specifically designed to provide **social security** and **old-age protection** to the **unorganized sector workers**, such as **domestic helps**, **gardeners**, **delivery boys**, and **street vendors**, who do not have any formal pension coverage. ***Hence, the correct answer is Unorganized sector workers.***

• The scheme is open to all **citizens of India** who fall within the **age group** of **18 to 40 years**. This entry age ensures that the subscriber contributes for at least **20 years** before reaching the **maturity age** of **60 years**.

• Under **APY**, a subscriber is guaranteed a **minimum monthly pension** of **Rs. 1,000**, **Rs. 2,000**, **Rs. 3,000**, **Rs. 4,000**, or **Rs. 5,000** after they reach the **age of 60**. The exact amount of pension depends on the **contribution amount** and the **age** at which the individual joins the scheme.

• The **Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)** is the **statutory body** responsible for the **administration** and **regulation** of the **Atal Pension Yojana** under the **National Pension System (NPS)** framework.

• **Government employees** (Option 1) are typically covered under the **National Pension System (NPS)** or other statutory pension schemes, and **students** (Option 4) are generally not earning members, making them ineligible for this contribution-linked scheme. ***Hence, these options are incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Successor Scheme:** The **Atal Pension Yojana** replaced the earlier **Swavalamban Yojana**, which was launched in **2010-11**. The **APY** was introduced to address the shortcomings of **Swavalamban**, particularly the lack of a **guaranteed pension amount**.

• **Recent Amendment (2022):** As per the **Ministry of Finance** notification, effective from **1st October 2022**, any citizen who is or has been an **income taxpayer** is not eligible to join the **Atal Pension Yojana**. This change was implemented to ensure that the **government subsidies** are targeted towards the **economically weaker sections**.

• **Contribution Mechanism:** The **contribution** is **automatically debited** from the subscriber's **savings bank account** or **post office account**. Subscribers can choose to contribute on a **monthly**, **quarterly**, or **half-yearly** basis to suit their income patterns.

• **Tax Benefits:** Contributions made to the **APY** are eligible for **tax deductions** under **Section 80CCD (1)** of the **Income Tax Act, 1961**, providing an additional incentive for **long-term savings**.

• **Death Benefits:** If the **subscriber dies** before the age of **60**, the **spouse** has the option to continue the account until the original subscriber would have reached **60 years**. If the **subscriber dies** after **60**, the **spouse** receives the same **pension amount** for life.

**Important Points__**

• **Nominee Rights:** In the event of the **death of both** the subscriber and the spouse, the **entire accumulated pension corpus** (the sum of contributions and returns) is handed over to the **nominee** designated by the subscriber.

• **Penalty for Default:** If a subscriber fails to maintain the required balance for **auto-debit**, banks may charge a **nominal penalty** ranging from **Rs. 1 to Rs. 10 per month**, depending on the contribution slab. The account is only **closed** if the **contributions stop** completely for a prolonged period (usually **24 months**).

• **Jan Suraksha Trinity:** The **APY** is one of the three **social security schemes** launched together in **2015**, the other two being **Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)** and **Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)**, collectively aimed at providing **comprehensive insurance and pension** coverage to all Indians.

• **Voluntary Exit:** **Voluntary exit** from **APY** before the **age of 60** is generally not permitted, except in **exceptional circumstances** such as the **death** of the beneficiary or the onset of a **terminal illness**.
</ul

questions.question: How does IMEC alliance benefit Indian exporters?

options.text: Reduced transportation time and lower logistics costs
Increased import duties on European goods
Limited access to Middle Eastern markets

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reduced transportation time and lower logistics costs**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC)** is a landmark infrastructure project aimed at boosting **economic growth** and **connectivity** between Asia, the Arabian Gulf, and Europe.

• The primary benefit for **Indian exporters** is the significant reduction in **transit time** and **logistics costs**. It is estimated that the corridor will make trade with Europe **40% faster** compared to the current **Suez Canal** route.

• By integrating **railway lines** and **ship-to-rail** transit networks, the corridor reduces the reliance on long maritime routes, thereby lowering **transportation expenses** by approximately **30%**.

• This efficiency makes **Indian goods** more competitive in international markets, particularly in the **Middle East** and **European Union**.

• The other options are incorrect because **increased duties**, **limited access**, or **higher tariffs** would act as barriers to trade, whereas **IMEC** is designed to facilitate and expand trade.

**Additional Information__**

• The **IMEC** was officially announced on the sidelines of the **G20 Summit** held in **New Delhi** in **September 2023**.

• The project is part of the **Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment (PGII)**, a G7 initiative to fund infrastructure projects in developing nations.

• The corridor consists of two separate parts: the **East Corridor** connecting India to the Arabian Gulf and the **Northern Corridor** connecting the Arabian Gulf to Europe.

• Key participating entities include **India**, the **United Arab Emirates (UAE)**, **Saudi Arabia**, the **European Union**, **France**, **Italy**, **Germany**, and the **United States**.

• Beyond transport, the corridor will also include **undersea cables** for data transmission and pipelines for **clean hydrogen** export.
</ul

questions.question: What does the Happiness Index primarily measure?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Subjective well-being**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **World Happiness Report** primarily measures **Subjective well-being**, which refers to how individuals evaluate their own lives and experience their daily existence. It is a self-reported metric that captures the emotional and cognitive evaluations of a person's life quality.

• The core measurement is based on the **Cantril Ladder** survey question, where respondents are asked to imagine a ladder with steps numbered from **0 to 10**. They rate their current life on this scale, where **10** is the best possible life and **0** is the worst. ***Hence, the correct answer is Subjective well-being.***

• **National income** (Option 1) is often measured by **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**. While the report uses **GDP per capita** as one of the six explanatory variables to understand why some countries are happier than others, it is not the primary definition of happiness itself. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• **Industrial growth** (Option 2) focuses on the expansion of the manufacturing and industrial sectors of an economy. While it contributes to economic development, it does not directly account for the social, psychological, or emotional health of the citizenry. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

• **Population density** (Option 4) measures the number of people living per unit of area. There is no direct or consistent correlation between the number of people in a given space and their reported levels of happiness or life satisfaction. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **World Happiness Report** is an annual publication of the **United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN)**. The first report was released in **April 2012** to support the **UN High-Level Meeting** on **Happiness and Well-Being**.

• The global movement to measure happiness was significantly influenced by the **Kingdom of Bhutan**. In the **1970s**, **King Jigme Singye Wangchuck** famously declared that **Gross National Happiness (GNH)** is more important than **Gross National Product (GNP)**.

• The data used for the rankings is primarily sourced from the **Gallup World Poll**, which conducts surveys in more than **150 countries** worldwide, using a sample size of approximately **1,000 respondents** per country.

• **Finland** has consistently secured the **1st rank** as the world's happiest country for **seven consecutive years** (from **2018 to 2024**). This is often attributed to the country's strong **social safety nets**, high levels of **social trust**, and effective **public services**.

• The report serves as a tool for **policymakers** and **governments** to shift their focus from purely economic indicators to more human-centric development goals, emphasizing **mental health**, **social support**, and **environmental sustainability**.

**Important Points__**

• To explain the differences in happiness scores across different nations, the report analyzes **six key variables**: **GDP per capita**, **Social support** (having someone to count on in times of trouble), **Healthy life expectancy** at birth, **Freedom to make life choices**, **Generosity** (measured by recent donations), and **Perceptions of corruption** in government and business.

• The **2024 World Happiness Report** highlighted a growing trend of 'happiness inequality', noting that in many regions, the gap between the happiest and least happy individuals within the same **country** is widening.

• Recent editions of the report have also explored the impact of **digital technology**, **social media**, and global events like the **COVID-19 pandemic** on the **subjective well-being** of different age groups, particularly the **youth** and the **elderly**.

• The **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, specifically **Goal 3** (Good Health and Well-being), align with the objectives of the **Happiness Index** by promoting holistic development that includes mental and emotional health.
</ul

questions.question: Which BRICS country is the largest producer of gold among the group?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Russia**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• Among the options provided, **Russia** is the largest producer of gold. As of **2022** and **2023**, **Russia** produced approximately **310 to 330 tonnes** of gold annually, making it the second-largest producer in the world, trailing only **China**.

• **South Africa**, which historically dominated global gold production for over a century, has seen its output fall significantly due to the depletion of shallow reserves and the high cost of deep-level mining. It currently produces around **100 tonnes** per year, ranking well below **Russia**.

• **Brazil** is a notable producer in the **South American** region, with an annual output of roughly **80 to 90 tonnes**. Most of its production comes from the **Amazon** basin and the state of **Minas Gerais**.

• **India** has very minimal domestic gold production, contributing less than **2 tonnes** annually. The majority of **India** gold is produced by **Hutti Gold Mines Limited** in **Karnataka**. Consequently, **India** relies heavily on imports to satisfy its massive domestic demand.

• While **China** is a member of the **BRICS** group and is the largest gold producer globally (producing over **370 tonnes**), it was not included in the given options, making **Russia** the correct choice among the four countries listed.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **BRICS Expansion**: The **BRICS** bloc, originally consisting of **Brazil**, **Russia**, **India**, **China**, and **South Africa**, expanded in **January 2024** to include **Egypt**, **Ethiopia**, **Iran**, and the **United Arab Emirates**, further increasing the group influence over global mineral resources.

• **Major Mining Companies**: **Russia** gold industry is led by **Polyus**, which is one of the world largest gold mining companies by reserves. Their flagship operation, the **Olimpiada** mine located in the **Krasnoyarsk** region, is a major contributor to the national output.

• **Witwatersrand Basin**: Located in **South Africa**, this geological formation has historically produced nearly **40%** of all the gold ever mined on **Earth**. However, mines here now reach depths of over **4 kilometers**, making them some of the deepest and most expensive to operate in the world.

• **Central Bank Reserves**: **Russia** has been one of the most active buyers of gold globally. The **Central Bank of Russia** holds over **2,300 tonnes** of gold as part of its international reserves to diversify away from the **US Dollar** and **Euro**.

• **Global Ranking**: On a global scale, the top three gold-producing nations are typically **China**, **Russia**, and **Australia**. These three countries combined account for a significant portion of the total global mine production, which is estimated at **3,600 tonnes** annually.

**Important Points__**

• **Kolar Gold Fields (KGF)**: Located in **Karnataka**, **India**, these mines were once the pride of the **British Raj** and independent **India**. They were closed in **2001** due to environmental issues and the diminishing grade of ore, which made extraction economically unviable.

• **Artisanal Mining**: In **Brazil**, a significant portion of gold is produced through **Artisanal and Small-scale Mining (ASM)**, often referred to as **Garimpos**. While economically important, these activities frequently cause significant environmental damage, including **mercury** contamination in **Amazonian** rivers.

• **World Gold Council (WGC)**: Headquartered in **London**, the **WGC** is the market development organization for the gold industry. It provides critical data on **demand-supply** balances, **investment** trends, and **Central Bank** holdings for countries like **Russia** and **India**.

• **Economic Impact**: For **Russia** and **South Africa**, gold exports are a vital source of **foreign exchange earnings**. In contrast, for **India**, gold is a major **import** item that significantly impacts the **Current Account Deficit (CAD)**.
</ul

questions.question: Why do seasons change throughout the year on Earth?

options.text: The tilt of the Earth's axis
The Earth's distance from the Sun

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The tilt of the Earth's axis**__

**__Key Points__**
__

• The change in seasons is primarily caused by the **axial tilt** of the Earth, which is approximately **23.5 degrees** relative to its orbital plane (the ecliptic).

• As the Earth performs its **annual revolution** around the Sun, this fixed tilt causes different hemispheres to be angled toward or away from the Sun at different points in the orbit.

• When the **Northern Hemisphere** is tilted toward the Sun, it receives more direct **solar radiation** and experiences longer daylight hours, resulting in **summer**. At the same time, the **Southern Hemisphere** is tilted away, experiencing **winter**.

• The **Earth's distance from the Sun** is not the cause of seasons. Earth reaches its closest point to the Sun (**perihelion**) in January and its farthest point (**aphelion**) in July, which contradicts the seasonal temperatures in the Northern Hemisphere.

• The **rotation of the Earth** on its axis occurs once every 24 hours and is responsible for the cycle of **day and night**, not the yearly seasons.

• The **Moon's gravitational pull** is the primary force behind the **tides** in Earth's oceans and does not influence seasonal climate changes.

**Additional Information__**

• **Solstices** mark the times of the year when the tilt of the Earth's axis is most inclined toward or away from the Sun. The **Summer Solstice** (around June 21) is the longest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere.

• **Equinoxes** occur when the Sun is positioned directly over the **Equator**, resulting in nearly equal lengths of day and night across the globe. These occur in March (**Vernal Equinox**) and September (**Autumnal Equinox**).

• The Earth's axis points consistently toward a fixed position in space, currently marked by the star **Polaris** (the North Star).

• Regions near the **Equator** experience very little seasonal variation because they receive relatively consistent direct sunlight throughout the year.
</ul

questions.question: The 'Mahalanobis Committee' was primarily associated with which Five-Year Plan in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Second Five-Year Plan**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Second Five-Year Plan**, which spanned from **1956 to 1961**, was primarily based on the **Mahalanobis Model**. This model was developed by the renowned Indian statistician **Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis** in **1953**. ***Hence, the Second Five-Year Plan is the correct answer.***

• The core philosophy of this plan was **rapid industrialization** with a specific focus on **heavy and basic industries**. It shifted the economic priority from agriculture (the focus of the first plan) to the **capital goods** sector to build a strong industrial base for the **Indian economy**.

• The **First Five-Year Plan (1951 to 1956)** was based on the **Harrod-Domar Model** and focused on **agriculture**, **irrigation**, and **price stability**. It did not follow the Mahalanobis strategy. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• The **Third Five-Year Plan (1961 to 1966)**, also known as the **Gadgil Yojana**, aimed to make the economy **self-reliant** and **self-generating**. While it continued some industrial themes, it was not the primary plan associated with the inception of the Mahalanobis strategy. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

• The **Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969 to 1974)** focused on **growth with stability** and the **progressive achievement of self-reliance**. It was launched during the tenure of **Indira Gandhi** and saw the **nationalization of 14 major Indian banks** in **1969**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis:** He is widely regarded as the **Father of Indian Statistics**. He founded the **Indian Statistical Institute (ISI)** in **Kolkata** in **December 1931**. His contribution to large-scale **sample surveys** and the development of the **Mahalanobis distance** (a statistical measure) remains globally significant.

• **Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956:** This resolution was adopted during the **Second Five-Year Plan**. It laid down the goal of a **socialistic pattern of society** and classified industries into three categories based on the degree of **government control**.

• **Steel Plants:** To support the goal of heavy industrialization, three major **steel plants** were established with foreign collaboration during the **Second Five-Year Plan**: **Bhilai** (with **USSR** help), **Durgapur** (with **UK** help), and **Rourkela** (with **West Germany** help).

• **Economic Targets:** The **Second Five-Year Plan** targeted a growth rate of **4.5%**, but the actual growth achieved was approximately **4.27%**. Despite falling slightly short of the target, it successfully laid the foundation for **India's public sector**.

**Important Points__**

• **The Mahalanobis Committee (1960):** Apart from the plan model, a committee was specifically appointed by the **Planning Commission** in **October 1960** under the chairmanship of **P.C. Mahalanobis**. This committee was tasked with reviewing the **distribution of income** and levels of living to ensure that the benefits of the first two plans were not concentrated in a few hands.

• **Shift in Strategy:** The transition from the **First Plan** to the **Second Plan** represented a major structural shift in **Indian planning**, moving from a **rural-centric** approach to an **urban-industrial** approach, which faced criticism later for neglecting the **agricultural sector** and causing **food shortages** in the mid-1960s.

• **Atomic Energy Commission:** The **Atomic Energy Commission** was also established during the **Second Plan** period in **1958**, with **Homi J. Bhabha** as its first chairman, further emphasizing the focus on **science and technology**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is another term for 'Budgetary Deficit'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fiscal Deficit**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **Fiscal Deficit** is the difference between the **Government's total expenditure** and its **total receipts** excluding **borrowings**. In modern **macroeconomics** and **public finance**, it is the most comprehensive measure used as another term for the **budgetary deficit** to indicate the **total resource gap**. ***Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.***

• It represents the **total borrowing requirements** of the **Government of India** from all sources, including the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, the **market**, and **external agencies**.

• **Revenue Deficit** refers specifically to the excess of **revenue expenditure** over **revenue receipts**. It indicates that the **government** is unable to meet its **day-to-day administrative expenses** from its **current income**. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***

• **Primary Deficit** is derived by subtracting **interest payments** on previous **loans** from the **Fiscal Deficit**. It shows the **borrowing requirements** of the **government** for the **current year**, excluding the burden of **past debt**. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***

• **Trade Deficit** is a term used in **international trade** to describe a situation where a **country's imports** exceed its **exports**. It is a part of the **Current Account** in the **Balance of Payments (BoP)** and is not a measure of the **internal budget**. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**

__

• **The FRBM Act (2003):** The **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act** was enacted to institutionalize **fiscal discipline** and reduce the **Fiscal Deficit** to a sustainable level, with a long-term target of **3% of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**.

• **Components of Receipts:** **Revenue Receipts** consist of **Tax Revenues** (like **GST**, **Income Tax**, and **Corporation Tax**) and **Non-Tax Revenues** (like **interest**, **dividends**, and **profits** from **PSUs**). **Capital Receipts** include **Debt Receipts** (borrowings) and **Non-Debt Capital Receipts** (recovery of **loans** and **disinvestment**).

• **Deficit Financing:** This is a **fiscal tool** where the **government** bridges the gap between **expenditure** and **revenue** through **market borrowings** or by **drawing down cash balances**. In **India**, this is primarily managed through the issuance of **Government Securities (G-Secs)** and **Treasury Bills**.

• **Impact of High Deficit:** A persistently high **Fiscal Deficit** can lead to **inflation**, a rise in **interest rates**, and the **crowding out effect**, where **private investment** is reduced because the **government** absorbs a large portion of the **economy's savings**.

• **Budget Presentation:** The **Union Budget** is presented on the **1st of February** every **year** by the **Union Finance Minister** in the **Parliament**, outlining the **estimated receipts** and **expenditure** for the upcoming **financial year**.

**Important Points__**

• **Historical Context:** Until **1997**, the term **Budgetary Deficit** specifically referred to the **net issuance of ad-hoc Treasury Bills** and the **drawdown of cash balances** with the **RBI**. This system was **abolished** and replaced by **Ways and Means Advances (WMA)** to provide **temporary liquidity**.

• **Fiscal Consolidation:** This refers to the **policies** and **strategies** adopted by the **government** to reduce **deficits** and **accumulated debt**. The **N.K. Singh Committee (2016)** recommended a **Debt-to-GDP ratio** of **60%** for the **General Government** (**40%** for the **Centre** and **20%** for the **States**).

• **Significance of Fiscal Deficit:** It is not always **negative**; if the **borrowed money** is utilized for **Capital Expenditure** (like **infrastructure** and **roads**), it can stimulate **economic growth** and create **productive assets** for the **nation**.

• **Data and Facts:** The **Fiscal Deficit** is usually expressed as a **percentage of GDP** to facilitate **comparison** across different **years** and **economies**. For the **financial year 2023-24**, the **Government of India** targeted a **Fiscal Deficit** of **5.9% of GDP**.
</ul

questions.question: Which one of the following defines elderly dependency ratio?

options.text: The ratio of children to the working-age population
The ratio of elderly (65+) to the working-age population
The ratio of elderly to children in a population
The ratio of urban to rural elderly population

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The ratio of elderly (65+) to the working-age population**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Elderly Dependency Ratio (EDR)** is a demographic measure that represents the number of elderly persons, typically those aged **65 years and above**, per **100** persons of **working age** (defined as those aged **15 to 64 years**). ***Hence, the correct answer is the ratio of elderly (65+) to the working-age population.***

• This ratio is a critical indicator used by **economists** and **policymakers** to determine the potential **socio-economic** support needed for the older population, who are generally considered to be outside the active **labor force**.

• The ratio of children (aged **0 to 14 years**) to the working-age population is known as the **Child Dependency Ratio**, which measures the pressure of the younger dependent population. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• The ratio of the elderly population to the number of children in a given population is called the **Aging Index** or **Elderly-Child Ratio**, which tracks the relative aging of a society. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

• Comparing the urban elderly population to the rural elderly population is a measure of **geographical distribution** or **urbanization** trends and does not constitute a dependency ratio. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• The **Total Dependency Ratio** is the sum of the **Child Dependency Ratio** and the **Elderly Dependency Ratio**. It provides an overall assessment of the total number of dependents that the **productive population** must support.

• A rising **Elderly Dependency Ratio** is a common feature of the **Demographic Transition** in developed countries, where **life expectancy** is high and **fertility rates** have declined significantly.

• Countries such as **Japan**, **Italy**, and **Germany** currently exhibit some of the highest elderly dependency ratios in the world, leading to increased fiscal pressure on **pension systems** and **public healthcare**.

• Conversely, many developing nations are currently benefiting from a **Demographic Dividend**, where the **working-age population** is large relative to the dependent population, creating an opportunity for rapid **economic growth**.

• The **United Nations (UN)** and the **World Bank** utilize these ratios to help nations plan for **sustainable development** and to design social safety nets for an aging citizenry.

**Important Points__**

• The **Old-Age Support Ratio** is the numerical inverse of the elderly dependency ratio; it indicates how many individuals of **working age** are available to support a single person aged **65 years or older**.

• In the context of **India**, the elderly population (aged **60 years and above**) is projected to reach nearly **20%** of the total population by the year **2050**, according to the **India Ageing Report 2023**.

• A high dependency ratio can lead to a decrease in **national savings rates**, as a larger portion of the **GDP** is diverted toward the consumption, **social security**, and **geriatric care** of the non-working population.

• To address the challenges of a high ratio, governments may implement reforms such as increasing the **retirement age**, encouraging **private pension schemes**, and investing in **healthcare infrastructure**.

• Demographic data used to calculate these ratios is primarily sourced from national **Census** reports and large-scale surveys like the **National Family Health Survey (NFHS)** in India.
</ul

questions.question: Name the Indian state that is the largest producer of mangoes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• **Uttar Pradesh** is the **largest producer** of mangoes in **India**, accounting for approximately **23% to 24%** of the total national production. The state benefits from the fertile **alluvial soil** of the **Indo-Gangetic plains** and a favorable **subtropical climate**. **Hence, option 1 is correct.**

• The state is famous for several commercial varieties, most notably the **Malihabadi Dasheri**, which has been awarded a **Geographical Indication (GI) tag** for its unique flavor and aroma.

• Major mango-producing belts in **Uttar Pradesh** include **Lucknow**, **Saharanpur**, **Varanasi**, **Bulandshahr**, and **Baghpat**. These regions are designated as **Mango Export Zones** to boost international trade.

• **Andhra Pradesh** is the **second-largest producer** of mangoes in the country, contributing around **15%** of the total output. It is famous for the **Banganapalli** variety. **Hence, option 2 is incorrect.**

• **Maharashtra** is globally renowned for the premium **Alphonso** (Hapus) variety grown in the **Konkan region**, but in terms of total **volume and tonnage**, it ranks lower than **Uttar Pradesh**. **Hence, option 3 is incorrect.**

• **Tamil Nadu** is a major producer in **South India**, known for varieties like **Totapuri** and **Neelum**, but its total production capacity does not exceed that of the northern states. **Hence, option 4 is incorrect.**

**Additional Information__**
__

• **India** is the **world leader** in mango production, producing more than **20 million tonnes** annually, which constitutes nearly **50%** of the **global mango supply**.

• The **Mango** (scientific name: **Mangifera indica**) was designated as the **National Fruit of India** in **1950**, representing the country's rich **agricultural heritage**.

• The **Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA)** facilitates the export of Indian mangoes to major markets such as the **United Arab Emirates**, **United Kingdom**, **Saudi Arabia**, and the **USA**.

• Nutritionally, mangoes are a powerhouse of **Vitamin A**, **Vitamin C**, and **dietary fiber**. They also contain **antioxidants** like **quercetin** and **astragalin** that help protect the body against oxidative stress.

• While there are over **1,000 varieties** of mangoes found in **India**, only about **30 varieties** are cultivated on a **commercial scale** for domestic and international markets.

**Important Points__**

• The **Central Institute for Subtropical Horticulture (CISH)**, located in **Lucknow**, is the premier research institution under the **Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR)** dedicated to the development of **mango cultivation** technologies.

• The **National Mango Festival** is an annual event held in **New Delhi** since **1987**. It showcases hundreds of mango varieties and promotes **agri-tourism** and **horticultural diversity**.

• Mango trees require a **temperature** range of **24°C to 30°C** for optimal growth. High **humidity** and **rain** during the **flowering season** (January to March) can adversely affect the **fruit set** and yield.

• The **States Reorganization** and agricultural focus in **post-independence India** led to the establishment of specific **horticultural clusters**, with **Uttar Pradesh** emerging as the dominant force in **mango production** due to its vast **geographical area** and traditional farming expertise.

questions.question: Who is regarded as the chief architect of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**B. R. Ambedkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dr. B. R. Ambedkar** is widely regarded as the **Chief Architect of the Indian Constitution** and is also known as the **"Father of the Indian Constitution."**
 
• He was appointed as the **Chairman** of the **Drafting Committee** by the **Constituent Assembly** on **29 August 1947** to prepare a draft of the new Constitution for independent India.
 
• As the head of the **Drafting Committee**, he was responsible for synthesizing various administrative and political ideas into a single legal document that governs the nation.
 
• He played a crucial role in ensuring that the **Constitution** provided extensive safeguards and guarantees for **civil liberties**, including the **abolition of untouchability** and the prohibition of all forms of **discrimination**.
 
• His profound knowledge of **constitutional law** and his advocacy for the **depressed classes** ensured that the document reflected a commitment to **social justice** and **equality**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi:** 
 
 
• Although he was the most prominent leader of the **Indian Independence Movement**, **Mahatma Gandhi** was **not a member** of the **Constituent Assembly**.
 
• His influence was nevertheless felt through the inclusion of **Gandhian principles**, such as the promotion of **cottage industries** and the establishment of **Village Panchayats**, primarily within the **Directive Principles of State Policy**.
 
 
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru:** 
 
 
• The first **Prime Minister** of India, **Jawaharlal Nehru**, moved the historic **"Objectives Resolution"** on **13 December 1946**.
 
• This resolution outlined the **ideals** and **philosophy** that guided the framing of the Constitution, eventually becoming the basis for the **Preamble**.
 
 
 
• **Dr. Rajendra Prasad:** 
 
 
• He was elected as the permanent **President** of the **Constituent Assembly** on **11 December 1946**, following the temporary presidency of **Sachchidananda Sinha**.
 
• He presided over the deliberations of the Assembly and later became the **first President of India** in **1950**.
 
 
 
• **B.N. Rau:** 
 
 
• He was appointed as the **Constitutional Advisor** to the **Constituent Assembly**. He prepared the **initial draft** of the Constitution, which was then scrutinized and refined by the **Drafting Committee** led by **Ambedkar**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Drafting Committee** consisted of **seven members**, including **K.M. Munshi**, **Alladi Krishnaswamy Iyer**, and **N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar**, with **Dr. B. R. Ambedkar** at the helm.
 
• The **Constitution of India** was formally **adopted** on **26 November 1949**, a date now celebrated annually as **Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas)**.
 
• It officially **came into force** on **26 January 1950**, marking India's transition into a **Sovereign Democratic Republic**.
 
• **Dr. B. R. Ambedkar** served as India's first **Law Minister** in the **Union Cabinet** from **1947 to 1951**.
 
• He famously described **Article 32** (Right to Constitutional Remedies) as the **"heart and soul"** of the Constitution because it allows citizens to approach the **Supreme Court** for the enforcement of **Fundamental Rights**.
</ul

questions.question: Under what circumstances can the Parliament legislate on a subject in the State List?

options.text: When Rajya Sabha passes a resolution

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**When Rajya Sabha passes a resolution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under **Article 249** of the **Constitution of India**, the **Parliament** can legislate on a subject in the **State List** if the **Rajya Sabha** passes a resolution.
 
• This resolution must be supported by **not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting**, declaring that it is necessary or expedient in the **national interest** for the Parliament to make laws with respect to any matter enumerated in the **State List**. ***Hence, the correct answer is When Rajya Sabha passes a resolution.***
 
• A law made under **Article 249** remains in force for a period of **one year** at a time. However, the **Rajya Sabha** can renew the resolution for subsequent periods of **one year** indefinitely.
 
• This provision highlights the **quasi-federal** nature of the **Indian Constitution**, where the **Union** is given overriding powers over state subjects under specific circumstances.
 
• Such a law ceases to have effect after **six months** from the date on which the resolution expires.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 250 (During National Emergency)**: 
 
 
• The **Parliament** acquires the power to legislate with respect to any matter in the **State List** while a **Proclamation of Emergency** (under **Article 352**) is in operation.
 
• Such laws become inoperative **six months** after the emergency has ceased to operate.
 
 
 
• **Article 252 (Request by States)**: 
 
 
• If the **legislatures of two or more states** pass a resolution requesting the **Parliament** to enact laws on a **State List** subject, the Parliament can make such a law for those specific states.
 
• Any other state can adopt such a law later by passing a resolution in its legislature.
 
 
 
• **Article 253 (International Agreements)**: 
 
 
• The **Parliament** can make laws on any subject (including the **State List**) for implementing **international treaties**, **agreements**, or **conventions** with other countries or international bodies.
 
 
 
• **Article 356 (President’s Rule)**: 
 
 
• When **President’s Rule** is imposed in a state, the **Parliament** is authorized to exercise the legislative powers of that **State Legislature**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the **Indian Constitution** divides legislative powers into three lists: the **Union List (List I)**, the **State List (List II)**, and the **Concurrent List (List III)**.
 
• The **Rajya Sabha**, acting as the **Council of States**, serves as the protector of the states' interests. Therefore, its consent is mandatory under **Article 249** to allow central interference in state subjects.
 
• During a **Financial Emergency** (under **Article 360**), the **Union** can give directions to states regarding **financial propriety** and the reservation of **Money Bills** for the **President's** consideration, but it does not automatically transfer the entire **State List** legislative power to **Parliament**.
 
• The **issuance of an ordinance** by the **President** (under **Article 123**) generally applies to matters on which the **Parliament** can legislate; hence, it cannot be used to legislate on **State List** subjects unless the aforementioned special circumstances (like Emergency or Rajya Sabha resolution) already exist.

5f
